title: Customer Churn Analysis Report
executive_summary: This report analyzes a snapshot of 749 customers, revealing an overall churn rate of 37.7%. Key drivers of churn include contract type, with monthly subscribers exhibiting significantly higher attrition, and a distinct at-risk segment characterized by high support ticket volume and low satisfaction. Lifetime value scales substantially with plan tier.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 749 customers with an overall churn rate of 37.7% and an average monthly fee of $42.11.
Churn rates are similar across plans, ranging from 36.6% (Premium) to 38.9% (Basic).
Churn rates remain stable across signup cohorts, fluctuating between 36.7% (2022) and 39.8% (2024).
Monthly contracts show a churn rate of 48.3%, which is 121.1% higher than the 21.9% rate for Annual contracts.
An at-risk segment of 100 customers (high support tickets, low satisfaction) exhibits a critical churn rate of 71.0%.
Customer tenure averages 20.8 months (median 19.0, std dev 13.2). Average satisfaction is 3.42, with 27 missing scores.
Lifetime value is highest for Premium customers ($1,817), which is 292.0% higher than Basic ($463).

limitations: The analysis is based on a single snapshot and does not track customer behavior over time.
Satisfaction scores were missing for 27 customers, potentially biasing the at-risk segment analysis.
Causal relationships (e.g., whether high support tickets cause churn) cannot be determined from this observational data.
conclusion: To reduce churn, strategies should focus on converting monthly subscribers to annual contracts and prioritizing retention efforts for the identified at-risk segment. The significant LTV of Premium customers justifies investment in their acquisition and retention.
